record.paper_title: Holomorphic mappings: Survey of some results and discussion of open problems
record.original_question: For a general holomorphic mapping f:C -> V from the complex line to an abelian variety V, and for a positive divisor D on V, must the image f(C) intersect D? The question excludes relying on the special case where f is a group homomorphism.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $V$ be a complex abelian variety of dimension $n \geq 1$, and let $D$ be an effective (positive) divisor on $V$. Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to V$ be a nonconstant holomorphic map. Without invoking the special case in which $f$ is (a translate of) a group homomorphism from $\mathbb{C}$ to $V$, must the image $f(\mathbb{C})$ intersect $D$? Equivalently, is it true that for every nonconstant entire holomorphic curve $f : \mathbb{C} \to V$ and every effective divisor $D$ on $V$, one has $f(\mathbb{C}) \cap D \neq \emptyset$?
artifact.status_search_result: By a theorem of Siu and Yeung, a nonconstant holomorphic map from the complex line to an abelian variety must intersect every ample divisor (in fact the defect vanishes). Combined with the classical Bloch theorem describing the Zariski closure of such an entire curve as a translate of an abelian subvariety, this resolves the question affirmatively for effective divisors on abelian varieties.

status_evidence.title: Defects for ample divisors of abelian varieties, Schwarz lemma, and hyperbolic hypersurfaces of low degrees
status_evidence.snippet: Siu and Yeung prove that the defect of a holomorphic map from C to an abelian variety A with respect to an ample divisor D in A is zero.
status_evidence.claim: Siu–Yeung established that any nonconstant entire holomorphic curve in an abelian variety meets every ample divisor.

status_evidence.title: Hyperbolicity in Complex Geometry
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses entire curves in abelian varieties, Bloch's theorem and intersection with divisors.
status_evidence.claim: The closure of an entire curve in an abelian variety is a translate of an abelian subvariety (Bloch), and Siu–Yeung's intersection result is now standard.
